security_audit.summary: Most scanner alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, relative links, localhost examples, and local capture paths. The launcher performs unattended npm package execution, while documented evaluation and reflection can alter a connected debug target. No prompt injection or data-exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: The compatibility launcher executes a registry package through npx with automatic confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Declare agent-lynx as a pinned dependency and execute its installed entry point, or require explicit approval before any registry download.

remediation.issue: JavaScript evaluation and ReactLynx updates can read or change application state.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation for evaluation and mutation, restrict use to development builds, and avoid returning secrets.

remediation.issue: App.CallStaticVoidMethod accepts class and method names for host reflection.
remediation.suggestion: Enforce a host-side allowlist of safe classes and methods, and require confirmation before invoking a reflection command.

content.user_title: Debug Lynx Apps with DevTool Workflows
content.value_statement: Lynx debugging requires coordinated device, session, protocol, and capture commands. This skill provides focused agent-lynx workflows for inspection, diagnosis, and testing.
actual_capabilities: Lists connected Lynx clients and active debugging sessions.
Sends supported CDP and App commands to selected targets.
Captures console logs, screenshots, heap snapshots, and performance traces.
Inspects DOM, CSS, runtime values, and ReactLynx component trees.
Uses snapshot references for taps, text entry, scrolling, and element inspection.
Documents programmatic connector workflows for custom debugging scripts.
limitations: Requires agent-lynx and a reachable device or desktop target with DevTool enabled.
Supported CDP methods vary by target type, platform, runtime, and build.
ReactLynx inspection requires a development build with compatible preact-devtools support.
Screenshots, traces, and runtime evaluation can expose sensitive application data.

use_cases.title: Inspect a Failing Interface
use_cases.description: Inspect DOM nodes, styles, console messages, and snapshot references on a connected Lynx page.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Runtime Performance
use_cases.description: Capture memory data and performance traces, then summarize the largest contributors and frequent events.

use_cases.title: Automate Device Debugging
use_cases.description: Use the connector library to select clients, issue protocol commands, and collect structured diagnostics.

prompt_templates.title: List Debug Targets
prompt_templates.prompt: List available Lynx clients and sessions. Explain which target is most suitable for inspecting the current page.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Visible Element
prompt_templates.prompt: Capture a fresh snapshot, find the element labeled [element description], and report its text, style, and actionable reference.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate a Runtime Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Collect error and warning console messages from [target]. Inspect relevant sources and runtime values without changing application state.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Performance Trace
prompt_templates.prompt: Record a trace for [workflow], save it to [path], summarize frequent events, and run focused Perfetto queries for suspected bottlenecks.

output_examples.input: Find the active Lynx page and inspect the login button.
output_examples.output: Selected the latest active session. The login button is visible, enabled, and mapped to snapshot reference @e7.

output_examples.input: Summarize memory usage for the connected application.
output: Collection completed for two Lynx instances.
The background runtime is the largest memory contributor.
The complete capture was saved to the requested local path.

output_examples.input: Trace the page load and identify expensive events.
output_examples.output: The trace was captured and verified. The summary highlights the most frequent events and the longest page-load slices.

best_practices: Select explicit client and session identifiers when multiple targets are connected.
Read the supported method reference before sending CDP or App commands.
Request confirmation before evaluation, reflection, navigation, or state mutation.
anti_patterns: Do not use stale snapshot references after refreshing the page or target.
Do not send Lynx-specific protocol methods to WebView sessions without checking compatibility.
Do not expose screenshots, traces, logs, or heap snapshots without user approval.

faq.question: What must be installed?
faq.answer: The agent-lynx CLI must be available, or it can be invoked through npx.

faq.question: Which platforms are supported?
faq.answer: The documentation covers Android, iOS, OpenHarmony, and desktop transports, with feature differences by platform.

faq.question: Does every target support all CDP methods?
faq.answer: No. LynxView and WebView targets support different methods, and runtime versions may differ.

faq.question: Can it capture screenshots and traces?
faq.answer: Yes. Captures are written locally and may contain sensitive application or user information.

faq.question: Can it change the running application?
faq.answer: Yes. Evaluation, navigation, App commands, touch input, and ReactLynx updates can change application state.

faq.question: Why can ReactLynx inspection fail?
faq.answer: It requires a development build, compatible preact-devtools support, and the correct active session.
